items.stem: Which safeguard most directly reduces the risk of dispensing errors involving look-alike/sound-alike (LASA) medications?

options.text: Using tall-man lettering and separated storage
options.rationale: Correct: tall-man lettering and physical separation reduce LASA selection errors.

options.text: Storing all medications strictly alphabetically together
options.rationale: Pure alphabetical storage can place LASA drugs next to each other, increasing risk.

options.text: Removing all labels to save space
options.rationale: Removing labels increases, not reduces, the risk of error.

options.text: Dispensing the larger package by default
options.rationale: Package size does not address LASA confusion.

items.explanation: Correct: tall-man lettering and physical separation reduce LASA selection errors.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A medication label states 'Store at controlled room temperature.' Which storage is appropriate?

options.text: Approximately 20-25 degrees C in a dry area
options.rationale: Correct: controlled room temperature is about 20-25 degrees C.

options.text: In a freezer below 0 degrees C
options.rationale: Freezing is not controlled room temperature and may damage the drug.

options.text: In a refrigerator at 2-8 degrees C
options.rationale: Refrigeration is a different storage condition, not room temperature.

options.text: On a sunny windowsill for warmth
options.rationale: Direct sunlight and heat exceed controlled room temperature and degrade drugs.

items.explanation: Correct: controlled room temperature is about 20-25 degrees C.

items.stem: Select TWO elements that a valid prescription for a legend (prescription-only) drug must generally include.

options.rationale: Correct: a valid prescription identifies the patient by name.
Correct: prescriber authorisation (signature) is required for a valid prescription.
A social media handle is not a required prescription element.
Pharmacy revenue is irrelevant to prescription validity.
Stock price has no bearing on a prescription's validity.

items.explanation: Correct: a valid prescription identifies the patient by name.
